title: dissector: Open Control Protocol OCP.1/AES70
description:
Added dissector for OCP.1 used for AES70 standard also known as Open Control Architecture (OCA)

This MR is about to bring in native dissection support for AES70, commonly known as OCA.

Just a quick review:
1. You 'say' noTabs, but your indentations are full of them.
1. Header fields should be initialized to '-1'
1. How is `hf_ocp1_params_time_ptp_negative` supposed to work without a bitmask?
1. How can `hf_ocp1_params_string` have ENC_UTF_8?
1. line 645: `if(!fname) return false;` in a function returning int is not allowed
1. `hf_ocp1_params_bool` without bitmask?
1. `dissect_ocp1_heur` this is not how you handle TCP packets, because a streaming protocol has no boundaries.
1. line 2015 and others: `return FALSE;` in a function returning int is not allowed
1. `decode_params_OcaMediaClockManager` for instance, defines not using parameter (`tree _U_`), then uses it anyway

added 1 commit
  • 35da7753 - OCP1: Dissector for Open Control Protocol OCP.1/AES70
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/5624/diffs?diff_id=304057617&start_sha=1116e57dd1d1e9a4e691650961a831a9a8d011ad)

@JaapKeuter 

Thanks for your review.

**1. You 'say' noTabs, but your indentations are full of them.**

changed modelines and cleaned up the code

---

**2. Header fields should be initialized to '-1'**

corrected

---

**3. How is `hf_ocp1_params_time_ptp_negative` supposed to work without a bitmask?**

This field is of type OcaBoolean which is represented as a byte instead of a single bit. Because of that FT_BOOLEAN and BASE_NONE is used. Isn't that the correct way? Tests have proven to be functional.

From `README.dissector`:

> FT_BOOLEAN  0 means "false", any other value means "true".

From AES70-3 5.5.2:
> The OcaBoolean datatype shall be marshaled as a single byte, where the value 0 identifies Boolean value false and
all other values identify Boolean value true.

---

**4. How can `hf_ocp1_params_string` have ENC_UTF_8?**

You're right, fixed.

---

**5. line 645: `if(!fname) return false;` in a function returning int is not allowed**

Fixed, also at different other points...

---

**6. `hf_ocp1_params_bool` without bitmask?**

same as 3.

---

**7. `dissect_ocp1_heur` this is not how you handle TCP packets, because a streaming protocol has no boundaries.**

You are completely right from a technical point of view. I wanted to postpone TCP handling to a later version of the dissector, but now it is included. (TLS is also another possibility)
Nevertheless, I'm facing the following problems:
- Heuristics are neccessary because there is no IANA port registered. AES70-3 5.1.3 states to use IANA dynamic port ranges.\
Some vendors seem to prefer port 65.000, but this is simply not reliable.
- Assuming no boundaries, there is only the byte-sequence `0x3b0001` which can be used for identification. I think this is not enough to make a reliable decision in an arbitrary tv_buff. Because of the protocol nature it is way more secure to let heuristics assume that a PDU starts at `offset=0` rather than test for the 3 bytes above.\
I've seen no real capture where this was not the case. An exception is for example a large fragmented Blob.

To let you know a bit more about the protocol layout, this is the public draft. Maybe someone has a better idea. https://www.aes.org/standards/comments/drafts/aes70-3-xxxx-151112-cfc.pdf

Please have a look at the recent commit.

---

**8. line 2015 and others: `return FALSE;` in a function returning int is not allowed**

See 5.

---

**9. `decode_params_OcaMediaClockManager` for instance, defines not using parameter (`tree _U_`), then uses it anyway**

fixed

added 1 commit
  • 16d29d52 - OCP1: Dissector for Open Control Protocol OCP.1/AES70
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/5624/diffs?diff_id=304064604&start_sha=35da7753cd51386ebcfb7f86c5ee6610a5a4736b)
Regarding 8: Have a look at [doc/README.dissector](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/doc/README.dissector) section 2.7 Reassembly/desegmentation for protocols running atop TCP.

Do you mean 7.?\
I don't understand exactly what I should change.

The current behaviour is:
1. `heur_dissector_add` for TCP registers `dissect_ocp1_heur_tcp`.
2. `dissect_ocp1_heur_tcp` checks if heuristic checks (`test_ocp1`) pass and then calls `dissect_ocp1_tcp`
3. `dissect_ocp1_tcp` uses `tcp_dissect_pdus` where `get_ocp1_message_len` returns the length of as much PDUs as possible to have as much PDUs as possible in one parent proto_tree.

The only function which is not stream compliant is `test_ocp1` because it assumes a fixed start boundary.

Differences I've seen are:
- `dissect_ocp1_tcp` returns `tvb_captured_length` instead of `tvb_reported_length`, I think this should be corrected
- `dissect_ocp1_tcp` has no additional check for minimum header length

Did you mean one of those?
